evidence: XEray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and highEresolution transmission electron microscopy (HRETEM) were used to examine the physicochemical properties of the film. The physical thickness of each layer was measured by spectroscopic ellipsometry (Nano View SE MGE1000). The chemical bonding states of the films and interfaces with the substrates were examined using highEresolution XPS (SPECS customized system) with a monochromatic Al Kα radiation source (hν = 1486.6 eV). The microstructures of films and interfaces were observed by HRETEM equipped with a field emission gun (JEOL JEME2100F). The film crystallinity was examined using grazing incidence angle XEray diffraction (GIXRD, D8 advance) with Cu Kα radiation at 1° angle to the surface. Capacitance–voltage (C–V) measurements were conducted at frequencies ranging from 100 Hz to 1 MHz, using an Agilent E4980A precision LCR meter. The leakageEcurrentEdensity–voltage (J g–V) and dielectric breakdown field of the films were examined using an HP 4154A precision semiconductor parameter analyzer.
